column2: On the authority of Abū Ruqayyah Tamīm ibn Aws al-Dārī (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The religion is sincere counsel (naṣīḥah).” We said: “To whom, O Messenger of Allah?”
He said: “To Allah, to His Book, to His Messenger, to the leaders of the Muslims and to their common people.” Reported by Muslim.

Al-dīn (“the religion”): the religion of Islam. Al-naṣīḥah (“sincere counsel”): clearing oneself of any deceit towards the one counselled. Qulnā (“we said”): we, the company of listeners among the Companions. “To Allah”: believing in Allah and denying that He has any partner;

[to His Book:] believing in the Qurʾān and acting on it; “to His Messenger” Muḥammad ﷺ: by believing him and following him. “To the leaders of the Muslims”: the rulers of the Muslims. “And to their common people”: all the Muslims.
The command to give sincere counsel, and that it was stressed so much that it was made as though it were the whole of the religion, because of its importance.
Sincere counsel is called religion and Islam.

A scholar should present an important matter in summary and then in detail, so that the listener is prepared and looks forward to the explanation of the summary; it then makes a deeper impression on the soul and is more likely to be accepted.
Sincere counsel is obligatory on every Muslim towards his Muslim brother in every situation, time and place.

Sincere counsel to the leaders of the Muslims means helping them in the truth, guiding them in what they do not know or have overlooked, keeping one's pledge to them and obeying their commands in what is right.

The noble Prophet ﷺ informs us that the pure and upright religion has commanded us to be sincere in our counsel; to believe in and acknowledge the oneness of Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, declare Him free of deficiencies and describe Him with the attributes of perfection; [to believe] that the Qurʾān is His speech, sent down and not created,

act on its clear rulings and believe in its ambiguous parts; to believe the Messenger ﷺ in what he brought, obey his command and avoid what he forbade; and to give sincere counsel to the leaders of the Muslims by helping them in the truth, guiding them in what they do not know and reminding them of what they have forgotten or overlooked.

We are to guide the common people of the Muslims to the truth, keep harm from them, whether from ourselves or others, as far as we are able, and command them to do good and forbid them from evil. What sums up sincere counsel to them is that we love for them what each of us loves for himself.
A man whose heart is not pure for Allah / is ill at ease under every onlooker's gaze;
and a man who does not travel with merchandise / to his other abode is no merchant.
I have counselled people and told them: / I am the warner, so let no one deceive you.
Gone is the one who gave sincere counsel to his Lord, his Prophet / and his leader, counsel whose resolve was fulfilled.
The righteous have departed one after another, / as if they were a necklace whose string has scattered.
